title: backlog.py done runs selfdoc stale over the item's own commits, so a stale doc is found by the worker, not at land
goal: backlog.py done ID runs python3 _tools/selfdoc.py stale --since <the merge base of the item's branch and the integration main> as one of its checks before the item's own, and refuses with reason class stale-docs, naming each doc and the code file that moved past it, when a kb/_self doc that map.csv maps to a file the item's commits changed is older than that change; the land step stale then never fires for an item done after this lands, and the digest's land.step failures of step stale fall to 0 the week after. One planted failure: a fixture item whose commit changes a mapped tool and no doc is refused at done with stale-docs.
notes: Premise (ops sidecars since 2026-10-05): land.step rows with step stale and exit 1: 7 this week, 13 all time; each is a landing the orchestrator ran, failed and handed back after the worker had reported done, so the fix costs a second worker turn. The reason class stale-docs is new: ql_capture.OPS_REFUSED (the closed classes of done.refused reasons) and the paragraph in kb/_self/querylog.md Surfaces that lists them change in the same commit, which is why _tools/ql_capture.py and querylog.md are in touches. Related: ST-atorqkvw (kb-worker rule 4 reads every doc stale lists) is the skill side of the same miss; this story is the tool side. Precheck 2026-10-08: both checks pass before the work: the planted failure (a fixture item whose commit changes a mapped tool and no doc, refused at done with stale-docs) is added to test_land_e2e.py by the work, and backlog.py check pins that the new reason class and the item files stay consistent.
